question: Why is some old glass purple?
notes: Narration v5. Times are seconds into voice.mp3, computed from words.json by shots.py. Each scene is one stop on the vertical paper strip. "paint" lists where the red-lead paint lands and the word it lands on.

scenes.line: Why is some old glass purple? It started out clear. Sunlight turned it purple.

art.desc: An old medicine bottle on the windowsill (from Short 02)

paint.on: fills the bottle on the windowsill

scenes.beat_note: Opens on Short 02's last picture: the thread. The paint drains out on 'started out clear' and comes back on the second 'purple'.

scenes.line: Newer bottles don't, mostly because of a machine that helped get kids out of bottle factories.

art.desc: An early 1900s automatic bottle machine beside an open-topped furnace tank
A boy of about ten (c. 1900) from behind, carrying hot bottles on a long fork

scenes.line: Iron in sand tints glass green.

art.desc: A heap of sand with a scoop; a few dark specks (iron)

paint.on: the iron specks in the sand

scenes.line: So glassmakers added a little manganese. Its faint pink cancels the green. They called it glassmaker's soap.

art.desc: A glassmaker's clay pot; a hand sprinkles a little powder in
A plain bar of soap with a few bubbles

scenes.line: But sunlight slowly changes manganese. Over months and years, the glass can turn lavender, then purple.

art.desc: An old bottle on a shelf in the sun

scenes.line: A half-buried bottle turns purple only where the sun could reach it.

art.desc: An old bottle half buried in the ground (cross-section)

paint.on: fills only the part above the ground

scenes.line: Why did the purple stop? World War One made manganese scarce.

art.desc: A World War One steel helmet

scenes.line: But mostly, it was machines. In 1903, Michael Owens got the first fully automatic bottle machine working.

art.desc: An early 1900s automatic bottle machine beside an open-topped furnace tank

scenes.line: Machines drew their glass straight from huge open tanks, where manganese was hard to control.

art.desc: A long, low open tank of molten glass; a machine arm dips in

paint.on: fills the open pool of glass

scenes.line: Most glassmakers switched to selenium. Selenium glass can age to a faint straw color, not purple.

art.desc: A glassmaker's clay pot; a hand sprinkles a little powder in

scenes.line: That's why purple glass usually means it was made before about 1920, when most bottles were still blown by hand.

art.desc: A glassblower from the side, blowing a bubble of glass

scenes.line: Owens had been one of those factory kids. He started at ten, shoveling coal and carrying hot bottles.

art.desc: A boy of about ten (c. 1900) from behind, carrying hot bottles on a long fork

scenes.line: His machine took over much of the kids' work, and helped end child labor in bottle factories.

art.desc: An early 1900s automatic bottle machine beside an open-topped furnace tank
The same boy walking out of a factory door into daylight

scenes.line: And why are maraschino cherries so red? That's another story.

art.desc: An old glass jar of cherries beside an old medicine bottle (bridge to Short 04)

scenes.beat_note: The tease: Short 04 is maraschino cherries. Old glass beside a jar of cherries: color hiding color.
